text:
Nia (AE): Hey team — handoff for ACME deal. They asked for a 3-week POC; legal pinged about KMS & data residency. Need quick alignment on acceptance criteria and eval harness scope.
Samir (DE): I can spin up a dedicated sandbox. Questions: do they want deduped golden prompts or a seed/variation set? Also need expected max seq len and QPS.
Riley (Solutions Eng): Recommend 2-tier goldens: 50 anchors (deterministic) + 200 fuzzed variants for regression. Scoring: 0.0–1.0 rubric per item, threshold 0.75 average, and no category <0.6.
Alex P.: Ops ask — we should plan for KV cache enabled + 8k context. Pricing-wise, if they exceed 500k tokens/mo we should propose Dedicated reserved capacity estimate. @Nia can you confirm expected volume?
Nia (AE): ACME expects ~120k tokens/wk during POC, maybe spike to 200k. So yes, include a 1-month Dedicated quote and hosted fallback plan.
Maria G. (Legal): KMS question: will customer keys reside in their KMS or ours? Also SOC2 + data residency EU-only. Need this clarified before any private deploy.
Samir (DE): For the eval harness: I'll check the model variants we can route to (fp16/qat). We should include automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if latency SLO is missed.
Riley (Solutions Eng): Proposal for acceptance gates:
- Functional: anchor pass rate >= 0.75
- Latency: p95 < 400ms for <= 4 concurrent sessions
- Stability: no more than 2 infra errors/day
- Security: legal sign-off on KMS and GDPR checklist
If any gate fails, rollback to canary model and trigger remediation runbook.
OpsBot: Deploy job queued: sandbox-dedicated-2209, est start 2023-11-06 09:15 UTC :gear:
Alex P.: On scoring: let's weight correctness 50%, hallucination 30%, instruction-follow 20%. We'll produce a CSV evaluator with columns: prompt_id, model, score_correctness, score_hallucination, score_instr, overall_score.
Samir (DE): Example eval command for harness:
```
python run_eval.py --prompts anchors.json --variants models.yaml --metrics csv --output acme_eval.csv
```
Nia (AE): Timeline draft:
Week 0: infra & access, security Qs answered
Week 1: seed goldens + scoring rubric agreed
Week 2: run sweep + customer review
Week 3: final report + pricing handoff
Alex P.: Dependencies/blockers: legal KMS ok, customer's test accounts, and sample production prompts. Flagging: customer wants SLA language in writing — who owns that? @Maria G.
Maria G. (Legal): I'll take SLA draft but need product to confirm uptime targets. Also need to review the security questionnaire (I'll annotate the SAML/KMS answers).
Riley (Solutions Eng): Action items:
- Samir: provision sandbox + model variants (owner) — due EOD 11/07
- Nia: confirm token volume & sample prompts — due tomorrow
- Maria: annotate security Q by 11/08
- Alex: prepare cost delta for dedicated vs hosted — due 11/09
Nia (AE): Thanks. If we can keep the eval harness focused (anchors + fuzzed variants) we should get decisive pass/fail. Ping me for any blocker updates. :rocket:
Samir (DE): On it. I'll post the initial anchors.json later today.
Alex P.: I'll draft the cost note and include burst to hosted fallback.
Maria G. (Legal): Uploaded annotated questionnaire to the shared drive, link: https://drive.redwood.example/acme-sec-q
Nia (AE): Great — let's reconvene tomorrow 10am PT. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
